messages:
anika_cs: Hey team — quick status from Tidelock week2. Go-live is at risk: audit logs still not showing up in their Splunk workspace and we have a KMS key policy mismatch with their infra team. Customer is worried about the timeline and Jordan flagged renewal sensitivity if we slip another week.
lee_network: Copy. Do we have the egress CIDRs they used for the forwarding lambda?
anika_cs: They used 34.205.0.0/16 for egress per their infra, but Splunk says incoming IPs are from our proxy pool (10.8.x.x) so might be NAT mismatch.
lee_network: If their NAT isn't whitelisting our proxy range that explains it. Can you share an example log/event id showing source IP?
anika_cs: pasted one below from Splunk ingest header: `src=10.8.12.45 dst=52.23.88.10 host=splunk-collector.tidelock.internal`
lee_network: Ok. Ask them to add our proxy CIDR 10.8.0.0/16 to their firewall rules. I can open a support ticket to request they confirm.
sam_kms: On the KMS side I saw a denied: `AccessDeniedException: Caller not authorized` when the forwarder tried to decrypt the envelope. Their key policy currently has a principal pinned to `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Tidelock-Forwarder` but our forwarder runs under a different role in their account.
sam_kms: Minimal fix: add this statement to their CMK policy (example):
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Redwood-Forwarder" },
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

sam_kms: Or add a cross-account role/trust so we can use the existing role name. Which option does Tidelock prefer?
jordan_am: Customer is leaning toward minimal changes on their side. If we ask them to update CMK policy it's going to their security review queue. Could we do a temporary workaround to avoid blocking go-live?

anika_cs: Two options I proposed in the call: 1) temporary S3 sink with server-side encryption managed by Redwood (we'd pull and forward to Splunk), 2) Spin up a dedicated forwarder in their account that uses the existing role name (needs infra sign-off but fewer policy changes).

nora_support: opsbot created ticket RW-30291 and assigned to lee_network + sam_kms. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-30291 :white_check_mark:

opsbot: Incident note: RW-30291 flagged as P2 (customer-impacting, go-live block). Added tag `renewal-watch` per Jordan's request.
jordan_am: Thanks. We should schedule a short sync with Tidelock security to walk through the CMK statement — that usually speeds approval. If we can commit to a temporary S3 relay by EOD we can avoid the renewal escalation.

lee_network: I can draft the firewall email and send to their network ops now (cc: anika_cs). Will include traceroute snippet and ask for our proxy CIDR whitelist.
anika_cs: Great — I'll draft the security-facing CMK policy change and the S3 fallback runbook. Posting both here in 20m.

sam_kms: FYI for the runbook: ensure re-encryption uses `aws:kms` and validate key aliases before switching. I'll add the quick verification commands.

anika_cs: Quick ask — can someone pair with me on a customer-facing note capturing risk + mitigation? Jordan, can you own the renewal escalation wording?
jordan_am: Yep, I'll draft and send to Tidelock leadership after our sync. Keep me posted on the S3 relay ETA.

nora_support: Follow-up reminder set for 12 hours. Ticket RW-30291 will update with progress.
anika_cs: Thanks all — I'll post the runbook + policy snippet once ready. :pray:
summary: Week2 Tidelock deploy blockers: audit logs not reaching Splunk due to NAT/proxy egress mismatch and KMS key policy misconfig. Customer renewal flagged as sensitive; team coordinating S3 fallback vs CMK change. Ticket RW-30291 opened.
